newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank sets repo at unchanged 4.35 pct.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank sets repo at unchanged 4.35 pct.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, Riksbank, on Tuesday set a new reverse one-week repurchase operation at an unchanged fixed 4.35 percent.
The operation will run from December 4 to December 11.
All bids must be left with the Riksbank by 0900 GMT today.
It was the second operation to be set at 4.35 percent after the Riksbank last Tuesday lowered its key repo rate by 25 basis points.
The repo is the central rate in a three tier system and the bank's key tool for controlling money market liquidity.
It has been cut aggressively this year from a starting point of 8.91 percent.

Economists had not expected any change in the repo rate this week but a poll by Reuters on Monday found a majority of analysts expect the repo to be lowered again on December 17 after the Riksbank releases its latest inflation report.
But 13 out of 17 economists surveyed forecast the Riksbank will lower its interest rate corridor at a board meeting on Thursday this week.
Twelve of those questioned expected a 50 basis points cut to the deposit and lending rates which currently stand at 4.25 percent and 5.75 percent respectively.
One economist expected at 25 basis point cut.
Four said there would be no change.
The interest rate corridors was last lowered on October 24.
